content_html:
Peru is considered one of the best gastronomic destinations in the world thanks to the diversity of its ingredients and the fusion of cultures in its cuisine. From the coast to the mountains and the jungle, each region has emblematic dishes that reflect its history and culinary richness. In this guide, we take you on a gastronomic route so you can discover the most authentic flavors of the country.

1. Coast: Flavors of the sea and Creole tradition

The Peruvian coast is known for its incredible variety of fish and seafood, in addition to the Afro-Peruvian and Creole influence in its cuisine.

Unmissable dishes:

  • Ceviche: The flag plate of Peru. It is prepared with fresh fish, lemon, chili, onion and cilantro. It is served with corn, sweet potato and mountain range.
  • Lomo saltado: A sautéed beef with onion, tomato and French fries, accompanied by rice. Its cooking technique comes from Chinese influence.
  • Tack tack: A mixture of rice and stews sautéed in a pan, often served with meat or seafood.
  • Carapulcra with dry soup: A dried potato and pork stew accompanied by noodles in basil sauce, very typical of the Chincha region.

Best destinations: Lima, Trujillo, Piura, Chiclayo, Ica

2. Sierra: The cuisine of the Andes and ancestral tradition

Andean gastronomy is characterized by the use of grains such as quinoa, tubers and beef, alpaca and guinea pig.

Unmissable dishes:

  • Pachamanca: A banquet cooked underground with hot stones. Includes beef, pork, chicken, potatoes, corn and beans.
  • Stuffed rocoto: A rocoto (large chili) stuffed with meat, cheese and egg, gratin in the oven. It is an iconic dish from Arequipa.
  • Cuy chactado: Fried and crispy guinea pig, accompanied by potatoes and chili. It is a delicacy in Cusco, Ayacucho and Huancayo.
  • Shrimp suck: A thick soup of shrimp, milk, potatoes and cheese, typical of Arequipa.

Best destinations: Cusco, Arequipa, Ayacucho, Puno, Cajamarca

3. Jungle: Exoticism and Amazonian flavors

The gastronomy of the Peruvian jungle is exotic and full of unique ingredients such as banana, yuca and river fish.

Unmissable dishes:

  • Juane: A type of tamale made with rice, chicken meat, egg and olive, wrapped in bijao leaves. It is the star dish of the San Juan festival.
  • Tacacho with cured meat: Fried and mashed green plantain accompanied by cecina (smoked pork).
  • Patarashca: Fish wrapped in bijao leaves and grilled with Amazonian spices.
  • Inchicapi: Thick chicken soup with peanuts, corn and cassava, very nutritious and traditional.

Best destinations: Iquitos, Tarapoto, Pucallpa, Madre de Dios

Tips to enjoy Peruvian gastronomy

Try food at local markets: They are the best places to taste authentic dishes at a good price.
Accompany with typical drinks: Don't miss the chicha morada, the chicha de jora or a good pisco sour.
Be adventurous with ingredients: In the jungle there are exotic fruits and meats that you will not find anywhere else.
Avoid altitude sickness in the mountains: Drink coca tea before trying heavy dishes.
